\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{اوسط} (ausat)}{اوسط (ausat)}]{\ur{اوسط} (ausat) — an average}

\label{lesson:UR-C350-ausat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a discovery, then the Urdu for to search out.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{اوسط}}
\textbf{\ur{اوسط}} — \emph{ausat} — \textquotedblleft{}an average\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اس} \ur{سال} \ur{بارش} \ur{اوسط} \ur{سے} \ur{کم} \ur{ہوئی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{is sāl bārish ausat se kam huī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This year it rained less than average.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{اوسط}} (\emph{ausat}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{awsaṭ}, \textquotedblleft{}middle, central\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ausat}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ausat}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{is sāl bārish ausat se kam huī.} — This year it rained less than average.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a discovery, then the Urdu for to search out, then say \emph{ausat} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{اوسط} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An average\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{اعداد} (adād)}{اعداد (adād)}]{\ur{اعداد} (adād) — figures (statistics)}

\label{lesson:UR-C350-adad}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to search out, then the Urdu for an average.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{اعداد}}
\textbf{\ur{اعداد}} — \emph{adād} — \textquotedblleft{}figures (statistics)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{یہ} \ur{اعداد} \ur{کیا} \ur{بتاتے} \ur{ہیں؟}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yih adād kyā batāte haiṅ?}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
What do these figures tell us?
\end{quote}

Masculine, used in the plural.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{اعداد}} (\emph{adād}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{aʿdād}, \textquotedblleft{}numbers\textquotedblright{}, the plural of \emph{ʿadad}, \textquotedblleft{}a number\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for an average, then the Urdu for figures.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{شرح} (sharah)}{شرح (sharah)}]{\ur{شرح} (sharah) — a rate}

\label{lesson:UR-C350-sharah}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for figures, then the Urdu for an analysis.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{شرح}}
\textbf{\ur{شرح}} — \emph{sharah} — \textquotedblleft{}a rate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{بینک} \ur{کی} \ur{شرح} \ur{بڑھ} \ur{گئی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{baink kī sharah baṛh gaī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The bank's rate has gone up.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{شرح}} (\emph{sharah}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{sharḥ}, \textquotedblleft{}an explanation, a laying out\textquotedblright{}; Urdu also uses it for a rate (of interest, of growth), a sense our sources do not trace.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ابھارنا} (ubhārnā)}{ابھارنا (ubhārnā)}]{\ur{ابھارنا} (ubhārnā) — to bring out; to raise (a question)}

\label{lesson:UR-C350-ubharna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for an analysis, then the Urdu for a rate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ابھارنا}}
\textbf{\ur{ابھارنا}} — \emph{ubhārnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to bring out; to raise (a question)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اس} \ur{تحقیق} \ur{نے} \ur{نئے} \ur{سوال} \ur{ابھارے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{is tahqīq ne naye savāl ubhāre.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This research raised new questions.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{سوال} \ur{ابھارا}, \emph{us ne savāl ubhārā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ابھارنا}} (\emph{ubhārnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{ubhārnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to lift\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{údbharati}, \textquotedblleft{}raises\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 2038).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ubhārnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ubhārnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{is tahqīq ne naye savāl ubhāre.} — This research raised new questions.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for an analysis, then the Urdu for a rate, then say \emph{ubhārnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
